units.text: INT. HOUSEBOAT KITCHEN - THUNDERSTORM - NIGHT
A narrow galley that rocks with each swell of the canal.
Copper pots hang from hooks and sway like slow bells.
A kettle sits cold on a gas ring.
Rain hammers the roof.
The lights have gone out, and a single oil lamp throws a trembling circle across the table.
BERNADETTE (70s, silver braid, wool shawl, hands knotted with arthritis) sits at the head of the table with a ball of yarn and two needles she is not using.
Her grandson WILLEM (30s, damp suit jacket, briefcase at his feet) sits across, rigid, his coat still buttoned.
His son JASPER (6, pajamas under a rain slicker, a flashlight he keeps switching on and off) kneels on the bench, his nose against the glass.
The boat lurches.
A pot swings and clangs against a hook.
Jasper yelps and flicks his flashlight on, pointing it straight at his father's face.
Willem lifts a hand to block the beam.
She watches them both over the rims of her glasses and says nothing.
The old landline on the wall rings.
A shrill, antique double-bell.
Nobody moves.
It rings again.
She puts down the yarn, eases from the table, shuffles across the swaying floor, and takes the receiver in a hand that trembles only slightly.
Yes?
units.name: BERNADETTE

units.text: Bernie? It's Arlo. I've been calling for an hour.
units.name: ARLO

units.text: The storm took the lines.
units.name: BERNADETTE

units.text: And the electric?
units.name: ARLO

units.text: Gone.
units.name: BERNADETTE

units.text: Is the boy there? Is Willem there?
units.name: ARLO

units.text: She glances back.
Willem has risen halfway from his chair, his jaw working.
Jasper has twisted around, the flashlight gripped in both small fists.
She turns back and lowers her voice.
They're here.
units.name: BERNADETTE

units.text: Tell Willem I said...
units.name: ARLO

units.text: The line crackles.
She holds the receiver away from her ear, then back.
...said I was sorry about the will.
units.name: ARLO

units.text: You can tell him yourself.
units.name: BERNADETTE

units.text: Bernie, put him on.
units.name: ARLO

units.text: She holds out the receiver.
Willem crosses the cabin in three strides, snatches it from her hand, and sets it to his ear.
Jasper switches off the flashlight.
The oil lamp gutters.
The boat tilts and rights itself.
Uncle Arlo. You have some nerve.
units.name: WILLEM

units.text: Willem, listen to me.
units.name: ARLO

units.text: No. You listen.
units.name: WILLEM

units.text: He turns his back to the room.
His shoulders rise, and for a long moment he says nothing at all.
Bernadette returns to her chair and picks up her knitting.
Jasper slides off the bench and crawls under the table, curling up at his great-grandmother's feet, where the flashlight, switched back on, paints a small yellow moon on the floor.
Say that again.
units.name: WILLEM

units.text: She doesn't look up.
Her needles begin to click.
